structure: Part 3 of trace:animals-fit: the delete-notification and cancel-amend features of the live-animals frontend. Read in full: cancel-amend.fit.spec.js (5 tests) and delete-notification.fit.spec.js (4 tests in 'delete-notification feature', 1 in 'delete-notification feature (submitted)'), plus all 10 trace zips the partition names. The bundled `playwright trace open` refused these zips (TraceVersionError: created by a newer Playwright), so each zip was unpacked into the part3 working folder (c1-c5 = cancel-amend tests :68, :82, :95, :111, :117; d1-d5 = delete tests :29, :45, :58, :77, :118, confirmed against each trace's context title) and mined with jq: every test step from test.trace, every request from the *.network files, and rendered DOM from frame snapshots. Refs below cite '<spec>:<line> trace' plus the test-step id (pw:api@N / expect@N) or the snapshot call id. Pages and order. Delete (draft): dashboard card (Resume, Copy as new, Delete links) -> GET /notifications/{ref}/delete 'Delete this notification?' (Draft tag strip, Back to /live-animals) -> 'No, return to dashboard' (link to /live-animals, notification kept) or 'Yes, delete notification' (POST, 302 to /live-animals?deleted=1, success banner 'Notification deleted', card gone). Delete (submitted): full journey submitted, dashboard card (View, Amend, Copy as new, Delete) -> same confirmation page with Submitted tag strip -> confirm -> /live-animals?deleted=1 banner. Cancel-amend: submitted notification -> dashboard 'Amend' (POST /amend, 302 to the hub, Amending tag) -> edit origin internal reference to DiscardMe99 (save returns to hub) -> 'Review and submit' -> review page with Amending strip and 'Cancel amendment' link -> GET /cancel-amend 'Cancel this amendment?' (Back to notification-view) -> 'No, return to notification' (link back to review, amendment and changed value kept) or 'Yes, cancel amendment' (POST, 302 to notification-view?cancelled=1: Submitted strip, success banner, original reference Imports456GB restored, read-only: no Change links, Copy as new and Delete buttons). Three axe checks (delete page, cancel page, restored review) each recorded an empty violations list. Conditional: the Draft/Submitted/Amending tag on the strip follows notification state; the Cancel amendment link appears only while amending. Not reached by any trace in this part: error states (stale concurrency token, failed delete), cancelling with no changes, direct URL access in the wrong state, Welsh copy, and the backend calls behind delete and cancel (the trace records only browser-to-frontend traffic).

claims.statement: Each notification card on the dashboard has a Delete action link that opens the delete confirmation page for that notification.
The dashboard Delete link's accessible name is 'Delete notification <reference>', the reference part being visually hidden.
A draft notification's dashboard card offers Resume, Copy as new and Delete actions.
claims.quote: Resume notification GBN-AG-26-2Y12DM ... Copy as new notification GBN-AG-26-2Y12DM ... Delete notification GBN-AG-26-2Y12DM

claims.statement: A submitted notification's dashboard card offers View, Amend, Copy as new and Delete actions, so a submitted notification can be deleted from the dashboard.
claims.ref: delete-notification.fit.spec.js:118 trace (d5) dashboard before delete (d5-dash.html); pw:api@132
claims.quote: View notification GBN-AG-26-3WE4AJ ... Amend notification GBN-AG-26-3WE4AJ ... Copy as new ... Delete notification GBN-AG-26-3WE4AJ

claims.statement: The delete confirmation page lives at /live-animals/notifications/{reference}/delete and is reached by GET from the dashboard link.
The delete confirmation page heading is 'Delete this notification?'.
The delete confirmation page warns, in one body paragraph, that deletion is permanent.
The delete confirmation page's primary action is a warning-style submit button labelled 'Yes, delete notification'.
claims.quote: <button type="submit" class="govuk-button govuk-button--warning" data-module="govuk-button">Yes, delete notification</button>

claims.statement: The delete confirmation page's secondary action is 'No, return to dashboard', a link styled as a secondary button that points to the dashboard (/live-animals).
claims.quote: No, return to dashboard

claims.statement: The delete confirmation page's Back link points to the dashboard (/live-animals).
The delete confirmation page shows a strip above the heading with the notification's status tag and its reference; for a draft the tag is a blue 'Draft'.
For a submitted notification the delete confirmation page's strip shows a green 'Submitted' tag with the reference.
The same delete confirmation page, with the same heading, body and buttons, serves both draft and submitted notifications.
claims.ref: delete-notification.fit.spec.js:29 trace (d1) call@2613 and :118 trace (d5) d5-delete.html

claims.statement: Confirming deletion submits a form POST to /live-animals/notifications/{reference}/delete carrying a CSRF crumb and a concurrencyToken hidden field.
claims.note: The crumb value is a CSRF token and is redacted.

claims.statement: The delete form's concurrencyToken suggests deletion is guarded by optimistic concurrency: the page carries the version it was rendered against, so a stale page could be refused.
claims.note: No trace drives a stale-token delete; see the gap claim on delete error states.

claims.statement: After a confirmed delete the frontend redirects to the dashboard with ?deleted=1.
After a confirmed delete the dashboard shows a success notification banner titled 'Notification deleted'.
The delete success banner's body reads 'The notification has been deleted.'.
The delete success banner is a GOV.UK success notification banner with role alert, shown above the dashboard caption and heading.
After a confirmed delete the deleted notification no longer appears on the dashboard.
When the user's only notification has been deleted, the dashboard list shows 'No Results' and an empty-state message.
claims.quote:
No Results

...

You have not started any notifications in this session.

claims.statement: Choosing 'No, return to dashboard' returns the user to the dashboard URL with the notification still listed.

A submitted notification that carries address-book parties (consignor, consignee, importer, place of origin, place of destination, contact address) can be deleted, landing on the dashboard with the 'Notification deleted' banner.

Deleting a submitted notification with address-book parties emits a NotificationSubmissionDeleted event whose party resolution needs the acting user's organisationId, which the frontend forwards to the backend; the trace cannot show this because it records only browser traffic.
claims.ref: delete-notification.fit.spec.js lines 94-97 (comment above the submitted describe); trace d5 network shows only the browser POST
claims.quote: Deleting a submitted notification carrying real address-book parties emits a NotificationSubmissionDeleted event that has to resolve those parties, so the backend requires the acting user's organisationId. This flow proves the frontend forwards it (EUDPA-389).
claims.note: The claim comes from the spec's comment, not from the trace; the sign-in in every trace uses organisationId=stub-org-1.

claims.statement: The delete confirmation page has no axe violations at WCAG 2 A and AA: the recorded violations list is empty.
claims.quote:
Delete notification has serious/critical accessibility violations.
Full axe violations:

claims.statement: The delete and cancel-amend confirmation pages use only GOV.UK Frontend components (back link, heading, body, button group, warning, primary and secondary buttons, tag) apart from the app-journey-strip wrapper that holds the status tag and reference.
claims.ref: delete-notification.fit.spec.js:29 trace (d1) call@2613; cancel-amend.fit.spec.js:68 trace (c1) c1-885.html
claims.note: app-journey-strip is a layout wrapper around a govuk-tag and govuk-body span; a standard tag plus caption could replace it.

claims.statement: Choosing Amend on a submitted notification's dashboard card POSTs to /live-animals/notifications/{reference}/amend and redirects to the notification's task list hub.
The dashboard Amend action is a form button whose accessible name is 'Amend notification <reference>'.
While a submitted notification is being amended, the hub, review page and cancel page show a yellow 'Amending' tag with the reference above the heading.
While amending, saving a task page (here 'Where is this consignment coming from?') returns the user to the hub instead of the next page in the journey.
claims.ref: cancel-amend.fit.spec.js:95 trace (c3) network after the amend POST
claims.note: In the same trace the first-time origin save redirected to /commodities.

claims.statement: While amending, the hub's 'Review and submit' button opens the review page at /notification-view.
claims.quote: Review and submit

claims.statement: While amending, the review page 'Review your notification' shows a 'Cancel amendment' link directly under the heading.
claims.quote:
Review your notification

Cancel amendment

claims.statement: While amending, the review page shows the amended values with Change links on every summary card and Edit details links on each party, and a Continue button.
While amending, the review page's Back link points to the notification's hub.
The cancel-amend confirmation page lives at /live-animals/notifications/{reference}/cancel-amend.
The cancel-amend confirmation page heading is 'Cancel this amendment?'.
The cancel-amend page explains that changes made since amending began will be discarded and the submitted version restored.
claims.quote: Your changes since you started amending will be discarded and the submitted version restored.

claims.statement: The cancel-amend page's primary action is a standard (not warning) submit button labelled 'Yes, cancel amendment'.
claims.quote: <button type="submit" class="govuk-button" data-module="govuk-button" data-govuk-button-init="">Yes, cancel amendment</button>
claims.note: The delete page's equivalent button uses govuk-button--warning; this one does not.

claims.statement: The cancel-amend page's secondary action is 'No, return to notification', a secondary-button link back to the review page (/notification-view).
claims.quote: No, return to notification

claims.statement: The cancel-amend page's Back link points to the review page (/notification-view).
Confirming cancel-amend submits a form POST to /cancel-amend carrying a CSRF crumb and a concurrencyToken.
claims.note: The crumb value is a CSRF token and is redacted.

claims.statement: Choosing 'No, return to notification' returns to the review page with the amendment still in progress: Amending tag, the changed value DiscardMe99 and the Cancel amendment link all still shown.
Confirming cancel-amend redirects to the review page with ?cancelled=1.
After cancelling, the review page shows a success notification banner titled 'Success'.
The cancel-amend success banner's heading reads 'The amendment has been cancelled and the submitted version restored.'.
claims.quote: The amendment has been cancelled and the submitted version restored.

claims.statement: After cancelling, the notification is back to Submitted: the strip shows a green 'Submitted' tag with the reference.
Cancelling discards the amended value and restores the submitted one: the internal reference shows Imports456GB again and DiscardMe99 is gone.
claims.ref: cancel-amend.fit.spec.js:95 trace (c3) expect@146, expect@147; c3-restored.html Import details card

claims.statement: The restored submitted review is read-only: no Change links, no Edit details links and no Continue button.
The restored submitted review offers a 'Copy as new' secondary button (form POST to /copy with copyOrigin notification-view) and a 'Delete' warning button linking to the delete page.

Copy as new ... <a href="/live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-5B6N3Y/delete" role="button" draggable="false" class="govuk-button govuk-button--warning" ... Delete

claims.statement: The restored submitted review's Back link points to the notification's hub.
The restored submitted review keeps the 'Review your notification' heading and the same six numbered sections.
claims.quote: 1. About the consignment ... 2. Description of the goods ... 3. Transport and arrival ... 4. Documents ... 5. Consignment parties ... 6. Contact address

claims.statement: No trace in this part shows the backend calls behind delete, amend or cancel-amend (which service is called, the method and payload, or how the snapshot is restored); the trace records only browser-to-frontend requests.
claims.ref: all 10 traces' network files: only localhost:3000 requests

claims.statement: No trace shows what happens when a delete or cancel-amend fails, for example a stale concurrencyToken or a backend error; no error page or message was rendered.
claims.ref: delete-notification and cancel-amend traces: no failed action, no error summary

claims.statement: No trace shows deleting a notification that is mid-amendment, or what the dashboard card actions are while a notification is in the Amending state.
claims.ref: delete-notification traces delete only Draft (d1-d4) and Submitted (d5) notifications

claims.statement: No trace shows the cancel-amend page reached by direct URL when the notification is not being amended, or the delete page for a notification the user does not own or that no longer exists.
claims.ref: all 10 traces reach the pages only through their links

claims.statement: No trace shows cancelling an amendment after making no changes, or after changing more than one section.
claims.ref: cancel-amend traces c1-c5 all change only the origin internal reference

claims.statement: No trace in this part renders the delete or cancel-amend pages or banners in Welsh.
No trace shows whether the 'deleted=1' or 'cancelled=1' success banner reappears on a later visit, or is dismissed after first view.
claims.ref: delete-notification.fit.spec.js:58 (d3) and cancel-amend.fit.spec.js:95 (c3) end on the first render
